name: MonarchAiGhostText
title: AiGhostText
wrapsNative: UITextView subclass in a UIViewRepresentable, with a second inert UITextView laid over it that draws the suggestion; UIKeyCommand, UITapGestureRecognizer and UIAccessibilityCustomAction; inlinePredictionType = .no
summary: A multi-line text field with inline completion: the model's suggested continuation is drawn in a muted colour after the typed text and is accepted by a tap, a button, or Tab on a hardware keyboard. MonarchAiCompletion is the headless state behind it.
whenToUse: For free text where the model can usefully continue what the person is writing: a reply, a note, a description.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single-line field with a fixed format, or for passwords: use MonarchTextField. Not for rewriting a selection, which is AiInlinePrompt. Not for chat prompts, which is AiPromptInput.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label and the accessibility label.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder text shown while the field is empty.

options.name: debounce
options.description: How long typing must pause before a request is sent.

options.name: minimumCharacters
options.description: The fewest characters before the cursor, without surrounding white space, for a request.

options.name: completion
options.description: Completion state you keep, to read or drive it. Replaces complete, debounce, minimumCharacters and isCompletionEnabled.

options.name: showsAcceptButton
options.description: Shows the "Accept suggestion" button under the field while a suggestion shows. Its room is always kept.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the announcements, the hint and the action names.

options.name: onAccept
options.description: Called after a suggestion, or one word of it, went into the text.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Called when the person dismisses the suggestion.

options.name: complete
options.description: Asks the model for a continuation of the text at the cursor, a UTF-16 offset. Return the text to insert, or nil for none. Its task is cancelled when the answer is stale.

states.name: idle
states.description: Only the typed text, or the prompt while the field is empty.

states.name: waiting, loading
states.description: Nothing is drawn while the request waits for the pause or is in flight.

states.name: ready
states.description: The suggestion is drawn after the typed text in the muted text role, and the accept button appears in the room kept for it.

states.name: error
states.description: Nothing is drawn. onError of the completion is called.

states.name: focused
states.description: The theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true): the disabled text and fill roles, no editing and no suggestion.

appearance: The box of MonarchTextField: the surface fill, the input border and the control radius, with the focus ring while editing. Typed text is the default text role and the suggestion the muted text role, both in the body type role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web wraps any textarea or input; on iOS the component is the field, because the suggestion must be drawn inside a UITextView. SwiftUI's TextField cannot report the caret or marked text on iOS 17, draw after the caret, turn off the system's inline predictions or take Tab from the focus system. The web's accept hint (a "Tab" key that is also a button) is here a tap on the suggestion itself plus an "Accept suggestion" button with a full touch target, since a key cap means nothing on touch. The keys are the web's: Tab or the forward arrow accepts, Control or Option with the forward arrow accepts a word, Escape dismisses; they need a hardware keyboard. The cursor is a UTF-16 offset, as on the web. Accepting sets the text through the binding, so it is not a step in the text view's undo history. The web's useAiRewrite and applyAiRewrite (rewriting a selection), exported from the same web folder, are not part of this entry. On the macOS host, which only exists to build and test the package, the field is a SwiftUI TextField with the suggestion laid over it.
accessibility: The field is one element whose label is the label and whose value is the typed text. The suggestion is not part of the value.
While a suggestion shows, the hint says how to accept it; otherwise the hint is the helper text.
A new suggestion is announced. The rest of one being typed through, or taken word by word, is not announced again.
VoiceOver has "Accept suggestion" and "Dismiss suggestion" actions on the field while a suggestion shows.

The accept button has a touch target at least 44 points high. The tap area on the suggestion itself is the suggestion's text with a 4-point margin, which is smaller than 44 points; the button is the full-size alternative.
The suggestion differs from typed text by its position after the caret as well as its colour.
Nothing is suggested while an input method is composing. The system's inline predictions are off in this field; the QuickType bar stays.
The text follows Dynamic Type and the layout direction; in a right-to-left layout the forward arrow is the left arrow.
edgeCases: A suggestion is only shown with the caret at the end of the text (white space may follow), never in the middle or with a selection.
The field grows with the typed text, not with the suggestion: a suggestion that wraps past the last typed line is cut off at the bottom of the field and still inserted whole.
Changing the text from outside, losing focus or disabling the field dismisses the suggestion.
A request whose text has since changed is cancelled and its answer ignored.
With a custom font family in the theme the field uses it; if the family is not registered it falls back to the system font.

The UIKit text view is compiled for iOS and has its own tests, but when this entry was written those tests had only been compiled, not run: the tap on the suggestion, the hardware keys and the alignment of the suggestion with the typed text still need a simulator or a device.
Experimental: the UIKit text view used on iOS has been compiled for iOS but not yet run on a simulator or device. It becomes available after the simulator tests and a VoiceOver check pass.

examples.title: Reply with suggestions
examples.template:
MonarchAiGhostText(
    {{label}},
    text: $message,
    prompt: {{placeholder}},
    showsAcceptButton: false,
    showsLabel: false,
    keyHint: "Tab"
) { text, _ in
    text.hasSuffix({{text}}) ? {{suggestion}} : nil
}
examples.code:
MonarchAiGhostText(
    "Reply",
    text: $message,
    prompt: "Type “Thanks” or “Let me know” and pause",
    showsAcceptButton: false,
    showsLabel: false,
    keyHint: "Tab"
) { text, _ in
    text.hasSuffix("Thanks") ? " for getting back to me so quickly." : nil
}

examples.title: Reading the completion state yourself
examples.setup:
@State private var note = ""
@State private var completion = MonarchAiCompletion(minimumCharacters: 1) { _, _ in " and so on." }
